references.text: Abraham was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold, reflecting the blessings of increased wealth.
The Lord had blessed Abraham abundantly with sheep, cattle, silver, and gold, as described in the promises of Deuteronomy.
Isaac was blessed with sheep, cattle, and many servants, an example of God's material blessings.
Jacob became very rich with much livestock, female and male servants, camels, and donkeys.
Job owned large amounts of sheep and cattle and was the most powerful man in the East.
The Lord blessed Job's latter days more than his beginning, with twice as much livestock.
Agur asked for neither poverty nor riches but warned that abundance could lead one to forget the Lord.
The warning continues that the heart can become proud when wealth increases.
Earlier promise that God will bless the offspring of cattle and sheep.
Silver and gold belong to the Lord, a reminder of the source of all wealth.
